nrIncident.summary: Reduced service between Sleaford and Skegness expected until the end of the day
nrIncident.message:
A fault on a train between Sleaford and Skegness means that trains fewer trains than usual are able to run along this route. As a result, trains will be cancelled and a reduced service will be in operation.
There are also engineering works taking place today between Grantham and Sleaford. Trains running between these stations will be cancelled and replaced by buses.
This is expected until the end of the day.
Customer advice:
Rail replacement buses are in operation as follows:
• 09:15 Boston to Sleaford
• 09:54 Sleaford to Skegness
• 12:00 Skegness to Sleaford
• 12:55 Sleaford to Skegness
• 14:15 Skegness to Sleaford
• 15:53 Sleaford to Skegness
• 17:18 Skegness to Sleaford
• 18:57 Sleaford to Skegness
• 20:22 Skegness to Boston
All buses running will call at Heckington, Boston and Wainfleet. Check journey planners before and during travel, your journey may be extended by 45 minutes.
Ticket flexibility:
If your train is cancelled, you will be able to travel on an alternative service operated by any other participating train company, either two hours before or two hours after the original departure time of the cancelled service, in order to reach your destination.
If you decide not to travel or cannot complete your journey due to cancellations, you are entitled to a full refund from your original point of sale.
For further information and guidance please contact your train company or speak to a member of railway staff.
Check before you travel:
You can check your journey using the National Rail real-time Journey Planner.
For helpful advice if you need to travel on a rail replacement service, including accessibility and bicycle information, please use our Rail Replacement Services page.
You can find the pick-up and drop-off location of rail replacement services by checking station signage or by searching for your station on our Find a Station page.
Please be advised that replacement vehicles may be busier than usual, and you should allow extra time for your journey.
Compensation:
You may be entitled to compensation if you experience a delay in completing your journey today. Please keep your train ticket and make a note of your journey, as both will be required to support any claim.

nrIncident.summary: Major disruption: no trains between London St Pancras International and London Blackfriars until approximately 15:00
nrIncident.routes: Trains between Bedford and Rainham (Kent) / Gatwick Airport / Three Bridges / East Grinstead / Haywards Heath / Horsham / Brighton, and between Cambridge and Gatwick Airport / Brighton, and between Finsbury Park and Sevenoaks, and between Luton and Elephant & Castle / Sutton / Gillingham (Kent) / Orpington, and between Kentish Town and Rainham (Kent), and between Peterborough and Horsham, and between Welwyn Garden City and Sevenoaks, and also between St Albans City and Sutton / Gillingham
nrIncident.message:
A tunnel being closed for safety reasons at Farringdon means all lines are closed. As a result, trains between London St Pancras International and London Blackfriars will be cancelled or revised.
Major disruption is expected until 15:00.
A visual disruption map video is available.
Customer advice:
No trains can run between London St Pancras International and London Blackfriars until further notice. You will need to use an alternative route to reach your destination.
You should allow at least an additional 60 minutes to complete your journey today.
Please talk to station staff, look at the information boards or check your journey planner for the most recent information.
How is the service changing?
While this disruption is ongoing, these are the following changes to services:
North of London St Pancras International:
• Trains that normally run between Cambridge and London Kings Cross will run as booked
• Trains that normally run between and Brighton and Cambridge will terminate and restart at London Kings Cross
• Trains that normally run between Bedford and London St Pancras International will have a limited service running two trains per hour
• Trains that normally run between Luton and Sutton will now run between Luton and Kentish Town. This service will be reduced to two trains per hour
South of London Blackfriars:
• Trains that normally run between Horsham and Bedford will terminate and restart at London Blackfriars
• Trains that normally run between and Brighton and Bedford will terminate and restart at London Blackfriars. This service will be reduced to two trains per hour
• Trains that normally run between Sutton to Luton will now run between Sutton and London Blackfriars. This service will be reduced to two trains per hour
• Trains that normally run between Horsham and Peterborough will terminate and restart at East Croydon
Suspended services:
• Services running between Sutton and St Albans.
How do I get between London Blackfriars and London St Pancras International?
If you are travelling between these stations, you will need to use your ticket on London Underground or London Buses.
This is also the best way to get to City Thameslink and Farringdon.
Please be aware that this will take up to an additional 30 minutes.
Can I use my ticket with another operator North of London?
You can travel on the following services at no additional cost:
• Southern services between Horsham, Brighton, Sutton and London Victoria
• Great Northern services between London Kings Cross, Peterborough and Cambridge

• Trains running between Bedford and London St. Pancras will have a limited service running two trains per hour

• Trains that normally run between Horsham and Bedford will terminate and restart at London Bridge
• Trains that normally run between and Brighton and Bedford will terminate and restart at London Blackfriars. This service will be reduced to two trains per hour

• City Thameslink
